Carla (Design): quick design review — dropped a new frame in Figma for the model catalog compare flow: https://www.figma.com/file/xxxx/model-catalog-compare Carla (Design): main asks: 1) filter chip density — should we collapse secondary filters under "More filters"? 2) performance badges — do they imply latency or cost? 3) version pin affordance — current pin icon is subtle Ben (PM): link looks good. i worry about discoverability if we hide filters. how many users actually use the extras? Maya (Product): analytics: ~12% of catalog users use >3 filters in a session. power users do. default should be flat, with a progressive disclosure for advanced filters Dave (FE): implementation note — collapsing into a dropdown saves horizontal space but adds a11y complexity for keyboard/aria focus. also hurts quick multi-select workflows Erin (A11y): agree with Dave. If we collapse, we must ensure the dropdown is reachable via single Tab and has proper aria-expanded/aria-controls. suggestion: ```
...
``` Carla (Design): good call. What about badges? Right now we have green lightning = "low latency" and a $ = "low cost". Are those intuitive? Ben (PM): users confused them in last test. some assumed green=better quality. we should add short tooltip text and a11y label Alex (Design Eng): tooltip + accessible name solves most issues. propose badge alt text like: "Latency: ~30ms (p50)" and "Estimated cost: $0.0003/token" Maya (Product): +1 on concrete numbers. but we need guardrails — numbers should be derived from a 1k token benchmark for fairness Dave (FE): UI layout thought — in compare table, badges should be inline under model name, not in a separate column. keeps compare matrix compact. mobile: collapse badges under a chevron Carla (Design): mockup updated: badges inline, small capsule tokens. pin icon moved next to version selector to make it contextual. wondering if the pin should be sticky on hover or persistent Erin (A11y): hover-only is not accessible. pinned state must be perceivable for keyboard-only and screen reader users. use text label visible to SR: `aria-pressed` on the pin button Carla (Design): good point. new pattern: - pin is a toggle button: `aria-pressed` true/false - visible text for SR: `Pin this model version` Ben (PM): rollout plan: A/B test two variants — (A) flat filters + inline badges + persistent pin, (B) collapsed advanced filters + badges in tooltip + pin on hover. track time-to-compare, #filters used, and mis-clicks Alex (Design Eng): dev question — do we have the backend numbers to show p50 latency per model version? if not, we should show badges as ranges (e.g., ~20-60ms) Maya (Product): infra can provide p50 per model over last 24h. will add an endpoint: `/api/catalog/model-stats?since=24h` Dave (FE): will need rate limiting and caching on that endpoint — avoid spamming on page load when teams compare 6 models Erin (A11y): small copy nit — badge tooltip title should be short, e.g., `Latency (p50): 32ms` and include `role="tooltip"` with `aria-describedby` on the badge Carla (Design): copy tweaks: replace "pin" tooltip with "Pin version for routing" and the confirm toast: "Pinned v2.1 to route: app-recommendations" Ben (PM): +1. also add an undo action in the toast for 5s Maya (Product): tracking: create a quick GD ticket for analytics events: `catalog.compare.open`, `catalog.filter.apply`, `catalog.version.pin` with properties Carla (Design): final ask — can FE and A11y pair on the dropdown/dense layout tomorrow? want to QA keyboard flow and tooltip timing Dave (FE): i can pair at 11am PT Erin (A11y): i'll join — bringing the screen reader checklist Carla (Design): thanks all — i'll push the updated frames and add the A/B test flags in the spec. :sparkles: Maya (Product): leaving a follow-up in the doc for metrics and hypotheses. :memo: Ben (PM): notes captured. if no major blockers i'll schedule dev spike next sprint. :+1:
